q: Is the paper's monotonicity lower bound dt*mu/h^2 >= 3 tight for the classical compact 4th-order Laplacian [-1,16,-30,16,-1]/12h^2, or is it specific to the paper's Q2 spectral-element alternating-stencil scheme?
basis: The paper proves this bound (Thm 3.9) for its Q2 stencil. Our replication empirically obeyed DMP in six runs, all of which happened to satisfy dt*mu/h^2 >= ~137 (well inside the bound), so we did NOT probe the boundary. A stencil-vs-stencil comparison with a dt sweep across [0.1, 100] * h^2/mu, checking min eigenvalue of the discrete inverse at each point, would isolate whether the '3' constant is stencil-specific.
next_steps: Build M = I - dt*mu*A + dt*s*I for a sequence of (dt, h) pairs and both stencils; compute min entry of inv(M); scan the (dt*mu/h^2) axis to find the critical value for each stencil; report whether the compact stencil's critical value differs from 3.

q: The 4th-order spatial rate saturates at ~6.8e-6 in our 1D convergence test because the backward-Euler time error dominates. If we replaced backward-Euler with a stabilized Crank-Nicolson or BDF2 IMEX and reduced dt to 1e-6, would the compact 4th-order Laplacian cleanly exhibit O(h^4), or is there a subtler h-dependent floor (e.g., from the manufactured-solution forcing evaluation) that would show up?
basis: Our order-4 errors are h-independent from n=32 upward, exactly matching a temporal-error floor. Which one it actually is has not been isolated: it could equally be the s * u stabilizer (added to both sides) producing an O(dt*s) contamination that scales with 1/eps.
next_steps: Add a BDF2 or a 4th-order Runge-Kutta ExplicitTimeStep variant to the solver; rerun the convergence sweep with dt=1e-6; also do a stabilizer-off (s=0) version for the pure-diffusion linear PDE and check that the pure spatial rate emerges.

q: The paper's DMP theorems are proved for the generalized Allen-Cahn *with* an incompressible convection field (u,v). Our runs used pure diffusion (u=v=0). Under a divergence-free rotating field (u,v)=(-y,x) on [-1,1]^2, does the compact 4th-order Laplacian (which lacks upwinding) still preserve DMP, or does it violate max|u|<=1 at some Peclet threshold?
basis: Convection-diffusion DMP is much subtler than pure-diffusion DMP for high-order schemes; the paper's bound-preservation includes a specific FD upwinding treatment of the convection terms (Sec 2, Eqs 2.6-2.7). The naive compact 4th-order Laplacian + central-difference convection has no such treatment and is well-known to lose monotonicity at high Peclet.
next_steps: Add a central-difference convection operator to the 2D solver; run at Peclet = h*|u|/mu in [0.1, 10]; record the largest max|u|; identify the empirical Peclet threshold where DMP first breaks.

q: The LiteLLM Argo-wrapper returned HTTP 502 with body 'Failed to parse upstream response: does not match any variant of SystemMessage | UserMessage | AssistantMessage | ToolMessage' for our judge prompt to argo:claude-opus-4.7, reproducibly, on two different endpoints. Which message-part variant is missing from LiteLLM's schema, and how many other subagent workflows in the X-100 project are silently falling back to gpt-5.4 because of this bug?
basis: Direct: we hit it reproducibly (3 retries, both ep). Anthropic's Opus 4.x class supports 'thinking' blocks and 'refusal' content types; LiteLLM's current Argo adapter probably only maps text and tool_use. Non-direct: the same failure would silently corrupt any long-form JSON judge prompt across the project.
next_steps: Instrument judge scripts to log which model+endpoint they actually used; grep the past week of subagent logs for the identical 502 body; file a LiteLLM issue with a minimal reproducer prompt; consider pinning argo:gpt-5.4 as the default judge across the project until fixed.

q: Our manufactured solution u_exact = 0.9 cos(pi x) exp(-t) is inside [-0.9, 0.9] for all t, so verifying max|u|<=1 on it is trivially satisfied and not really a DMP stress test. A traveling-front manufactured solution u_exact = tanh((x - c*t)/sqrt(2*eps)) drives values arbitrarily close to +/-1 and passes through the boundary of the DMP set. Would the compact 4th-order Laplacian preserve DMP under such a solution as h and eps are varied simultaneously, and where does DMP first fail?
basis: The paper's own DMP examples (Fig 6.x) use exactly this front-like initial data. Our runs used random IC in [-0.9, 0.9] which stays comfortably inside the DMP set - so we did NOT stress-test the boundary in the way the paper's examples do.
next_steps: Add a traveling-front IC + forcing that makes u_exact = tanh(...) an exact solution; rerun DMP dynamics with the compact stencil at eps in {0.01, 0.005, 0.001}, h in {1/64, 1/128, 1/256}; plot the maximum overshoot max(max|u^n|) - 1 as a function of (h, eps); identify the (h, eps) locus where overshoot first exceeds machine epsilon.
